messages:
jen-support: FYI customer acme-prod opened a ticket, p99 on /v1/generate jumped from ~400ms to ~2.1s around 09:02PT. They pasted graphs + traces. says this started after a small config change yesterday :grimacing:
kevin-sre: can you drop the trace id and some logs? likely continuous-batcher timeout oscillation. cc @maria-ops :eyes:
jen-support: trace id 8f3a2b, logs show a bunch of requests hitting batcher wait path then timing out and falling back, lots of single-token requests in the mix. attaching snippet: 
```
# sample from service logs
ts=2026-03-12T09:02:11Z tenant=acme-prod request_id=8f3a2b path=/v1/generate batch_wait_ms=25 outcome=timeout fallback=single
ts=2026-03-12T09:02:11Z tenant=acme-prod request_id=8f3a2c path=/v1/generate batch_wait_ms=25 outcome=batched size=4
```
kevin-sre: that matches a classic tiny-requests + batch-timeout tradeoff. p95 fine but p99 skyrocket when tiny concurrent bursts cause many small batches to hit timeout then serialize. we should test lowering batch_wait_ms and enabling immediate-fallback for tiny payloads.
maria-ops: agree. quick mitigation: reduce batch_wait_ms from 25 -> 8 for acme-prod and enable "fast-path" for payloads < 128 tokens. I'll canary to 10% first. use rctl to patch.
sam-dev: repro steps (what I ran locally):
1) spawn 150 concurrent 20B payloads (short prompts) with 100ms inter-arrival jitter
2) run: `wrk -t8 -c150 -d60s --latency --script tiny-prompts.lua http://ingress/acme/v1/generate`
3) observe many 20-40ms batches but tail spikes ~2s when batcher times out and falls back
(attach trace ids)
kevin-sre: thanks. quick patch command I ran in staging: 
```
rctl rollout-batcher --tenant acme-prod --set "batch_policy.batch_wait_ms=8" --set "batch_policy.fast_path_threshold_tokens=128" --canary 5% --timeout 5m
```
deploy-bot: Starting rollout: rollout-id=rl-20260312-007 tenant=acme-prod canary=5% initiated_by=kevin-sre
alerts-bot: metric alert suppressed for rollout rl-20260312-007 (expected transient change)
jen-support: applied to canary, sent repro to customer, will monitor. customer says they can try load test in 10m. :thumbsup:
maria-ops: monitor tips: watch batcher.queue_depth, batch_size_histogram, fallback_rate, instance_cpu. If fallback_rate drops and p99 improves we ramp. if not revert.
jen-support: update — after canary p99 dropped from 2.1s -> 740ms on canary hosts. customer ran a test and saw similar improvement. rolling to 30% now.
kevin-sre: longer-term item: we need adaptive timeout that looks at recent tiny-payload fraction and short-circuits batch_wait for known high tiny-request patterns. filed ENG-1248.
sam-dev: created a small test harness in repo: `tools/bench/tiny-burst-repro` to help validate. PR incoming.
maria-ops: rolling to 100% now. deploy-bot: Rollout rl-20260312-007 progressed: 30% -> 100% success.
jen-support: customer confirms production p99 back to ~600-800ms and ticket updated. closing once they ack in 24h. thanks team :heart:
kevin-sre: follow-ups: add runbook entry (eng-runbooks/batcher-timeout-oscillation.md), add grafana alert for fallback_rate > 0.5% sustained, and add a smoke test in CI that exercises tiny-burst pattern.
jen-support: noted, will add to the ticket and move to postmortem if they re-open.
